subtopics.title: Three Highs by Name, Place and Character

questions.question: The three subtropical anticyclones that control South Africa's weather are the:
options: South Atlantic High, South Indian High and Kalahari High
Benguela High, Agulhas High and Karoo High
Cape High, Natal High and Highveld High
Equatorial High, Polar High and Coastal High

questions.question: In the Southern Hemisphere, air circulates around a high-pressure cell:
options: Clockwise
Anticlockwise
Straight outward with no rotation
Anticlockwise in summer only

questions.question: The west coast near Port Nolloth gets fog banks rather than rain clouds mainly because:
options: The escarpment blocks all cloud
The Agulhas current warms the air too much
The South Atlantic High drives cold Benguela water along the coast, so evaporation is too weak to feed rain
The Kalahari High sits over the ocean there

questions.question: Which weather character do all three highs share?
options: Rising, converging, unstable air with thick cloud
Strong rotation around a warm central eye
Continuous drizzle and low stratus
Subsiding, diverging air that warms by compression, giving stable, clear conditions

subtopics.title: How the Highs Run South Africa's Seasons

questions.question: In winter, the interior plateau stays dry because the inversion layer:
options: Lies below the level of the escarpment, so moist maritime air cannot climb onto the plateau
Rises far above the escarpment
Disappears completely
Moves out over the Indian Ocean

questions.question: Summer thunderstorms return to the plateau when:
options: The Benguela current warms up
The Kalahari High strengthens at the surface
Surface heating weakens the Kalahari High and the inversion lifts above the escarpment, letting moist air stream in
Cold fronts cross the interior daily

questions.question: The Cape receives frontal rain in winter because the pressure belt:
options: Stops moving in winter
Migrates north with the overhead sun, uncovering the south-western corner so cold fronts can swing beneath the continent
Migrates south, dragging the fronts north
Reverses its rotation in winter

questions.question: A ridging South Atlantic High brings rain to the south coast by:
options: Lifting the inversion over the plateau
Blocking the Agulhas current
Creating a berg wind
Extending a tongue of high pressure around the southern tip that pushes cool, moist maritime air onshore

subtopics.title: The Travelling Disturbances — Moisture Front, Coastal Low, Berg Wind

questions.question: The moisture front over the summer interior is the boundary between:
options: Polar air and tropical air
The Benguela and Agulhas currents
Humid tropical air from the north-east and hot, dry air over the western interior
Winter and summer air masses

questions.question: As a coastal low passes a town, the weather changes from:
options: Hot, dry offshore wind ahead of it to cool, moist onshore air behind it
Cool onshore air ahead of it to hot offshore wind behind it
Thunderstorms to snow
Fog to heatwave permanently

questions.question: Air descending 1 500 m off the plateau in a berg wind warms by roughly:
options: Two degrees Celsius
Fourteen to fifteen degrees Celsius, at about one degree per hundred metres of descent
Fifty degrees Celsius
It cools rather than warms

questions.question: Berg-wind days carry the country's highest fire danger because they combine:
options: Heavy rain and lightning
Cold air and thick fog
High humidity and calm air
Hot temperatures, very low humidity and strong gusty offshore wind over dry winter fuel

subtopics.title: Reading It All on the Synoptic Chart

questions.question: A strong closed high of more than 1 024 hPa sitting over the interior plateau on a synoptic chart indicates:
options: A winter chart, with the Kalahari High at full strength
A summer chart with a heat low
An approaching tropical cyclone
A moisture front over the plateau

questions.question: Interior stations reporting dew points in the teens, with a heat low over the north-western interior, identify the chart as:
options: A winter chart
A chart showing berg-wind conditions nationwide
A summer chart with moist air feeding thunderstorms
Impossible to date

questions.question: After a cold front exits, ridging appears on the chart as:
options: A new low forming over the plateau
The South Atlantic High's isobars bulging eastward around the south coast like a hook
Isobars vanishing over the ocean
The Kalahari High moving out to sea

questions.question: Coastal stations ahead of a coastal low reporting hot, dry offshore winds tell you that:
options: A tropical cyclone is making landfall
The inversion has broken
Ridging is complete
Berg-wind conditions prevail, and an abrupt cool change will follow the low's passage

questions.question: In the picture of three guards around the property, the guards stand for:
options: The South Atlantic High, the South Indian High and the Kalahari High
Three cold fronts
The three capital cities
Three ocean currents

questions.question: Sinking air in a high-pressure cell destroys cloud because:
options: It spins the cloud apart
It freezes the cloud droplets
Sinking air is compressed and warms, evaporating cloud like a warm cloth wiping steam off a mirror
It pushes cloud into the ocean

questions.question: The sea at Langebaan is cold while the sea at Margate is warm because:
options: Margate is closer to the equator by a thousand kilometres
The west-side guard drives the cold Benguela current while the east-side guard drives the warm Agulhas current
The Atlantic is always frozen
Rivers cool the west coast

questions.question: In the pot-lid picture, the lid stands for:
options: The escarpment
The Agulhas current
The moisture front
The inversion layer of warm air created by sinking air over the plateau

questions.question: In winter, moist sea air cannot reach the plateau because:
options: The lid sits below the top of the escarpment step, refusing it entry
The sea stops evaporating in winter
The wind only blows offshore in winter
The plateau is too cold for air to move

questions.question: The flat brown haze over interior towns on winter mornings is:
options: Sea fog from the coast
Dust and smoke trapped beneath the low winter inversion — the lid made visible
Cloud forming along the moisture front
Smoke from summer wildfires

questions.question: Line thunderstorms form along the moisture front because:
options: The lid presses down hardest there
Cold fronts cross the plateau there
Incoming moist air meets dry desert air along a boundary and is forced to rise, so storms queue along the line
The escarpment forces air to sink there

subtopics.title: The Hairdryer Wind and the Cool Change

questions.question: The berg wind is called the hairdryer because plateau air:
options: Rises and cools over the mountains
Circles the coast without changing
Picks up moisture from the sea
Falls about 1 500 m off the escarpment, warming roughly a degree per hundred metres, and arrives hot, dry and gusty

questions.question: A mid-thirties July afternoon in East London while the plateau sits near freezing is explained by:
options: Berg-wind conditions — compressed, descending plateau air arriving at the coast
The Benguela current warming suddenly
A tropical cyclone offshore
The inversion lifting in winter

questions.question: Behind the sliding bead of the coastal low, a town experiences:
options: Hotter, drier wind than before
Cool, damp onshore air — often ten degrees colder within an hour, with low cloud and drizzle
A thunderstorm line
No change at all

questions.question: Which set of actions belongs to a declared berg-wind fire-danger day?
options: Open braais and crop burning as usual
Evacuating the plateau
Total fire bans, firebreaks prepared, warnings broadcast and crews on standby
Closing storm-water drains
